title: Vector service operational contract: latency bands, error budgets, and traffic-shift rollback criteria
creator: Ravi Menon
description: Purpose: define concrete SLA/SLO targets, error budgets, and progressive rollout/rollback gates for the multi-tenant vector (embeddings + reranking) inference service. This ticket captures technical SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency for typical request sizes), availability targets, acceptable error classes, automatic and manual rollback gates for canary/capacity ramp-ups, and runbook links for operational response.
background: The vector service has seen variable tail latency under mixed workloads (short single-vector queries + batch upsert loads). Product teams want a clearly defined operational contract so integrations (hosted API, dedicated pools, and private deployment) can instrument alerts and calibrate client-side timeouts. Existing tickets touched SLOs for embeddings at a high level but lacked rollout gating thresholds and explicit degradation policies for multi-tenant behavior.
goals: 1) Define quantifiable latency envelopes for small/median/large vectors; 2) Establish availability SLO and monthly error budget; 3) Specify automatic canary acceptance and progressive traffic-shift gates (with rollback thresholds); 4) Produce acceptance criteria and runbook snippets for on-call and release owners; 5) Align with Dedicated and Private leads on per-tenant stricter SLAs.
non_goals: This ticket does not implement instrumentation or alerting (ENG tickets will do that), and it does not change model architectures or quantization configs. It also does not set pricing or contractual enterprise SLAs beyond a reference template.
slo_definitions: P50 latency (64-dim vector query, 1-2 nearest neighbors): <= 18 ms
Availability (request success without 5xx for API-level calls): 99.95% monthly
Error budget: 0.05% of requests per calendar month (includes 5xx and persistent timeouts > 5s)
Throughput target under dedicated baseline: sustain 1.2k qps per GPU pool with median latency within P95 target
error_classification: Transient 429/503 due to autoscaling burst: considered degraded but tolerable if short-lived (<5 minutes)
Persistent 5xx from model runtime (same error class repeating >1% of requests over 10m): counts against error budget
Client-side timeouts (<= 1% of requests due to network flakiness) are excluded from platform error budget if traced to customer network
Incorrect vector responses (semantic regressions) are measured via quality evaluations and flagged outside this ticket for quality SLOs
rollout_gates: Canary stage (0->5% traffic): require no new P99 violations above baseline for 30m, and error budget burn <= 5% relative to baseline for 60m
Staged ramp (5->25%): require P95 <= 1.25x baseline and error budget burn <= 20% over a rolling 2h window
General availability (>25%): require P95 <= baseline target and monthly projected error budget burn <= 50%
Automatic rollback trigger: sustained P99 > 2x baseline for 10 minutes OR error budget burn rate projecting >100% by month-end => auto-rollback to previous model/variant
Manual escalation gate: when automatic rollback fires, on-call and release owner notified; manual hold required for region-wide traffic shifts or dedicated tenant migrations
acceptance_criteria: PRD reviewed and approved by Engineering leads (Serving Runtime, Autoscaler) and SRE
SLOs documented in the public SLO registry and added to observability dashboards (latency percentiles, error budget burn) with panel links
Rollout gating logic implemented as automated checks in release pipeline (CI/CD) or configured in Console for staged traffic shifts
Runbook pages created with exact thresholds, playbook steps for rollback, and contact rotations for escalations
Dedicated and Private product contacts have confirmed per-tenant stricter thresholds and sign-off process documented
risk_mitigation: Add short-lived aggressive autoscaling capacity reserve during first two weekends of GA to avoid noisy neighbor surprises
Enable prefix caching for high-frequency vector queries to reduce tail exposure during ramp
Create synthetic load tests that combine upsert-heavy backfills with real-time queries to validate mixed-workload SLOs before live rollout
open_questions: What is the authoritative baseline for 'baseline' percentiles? (answer: use week-over-week median of last 30 days once instrumentation is complete)
Should we treat 429s from throttling as error-budget-eligible for Hosted customers? (proposal: count above configured quota for the tenant only)
Who owns automated rollback in Private customers where control plane is customer-operated? (ops: provide guardrail config and documentation; manual rollback still required)
How to reconcile differing per-tenant SLAs in Dedicated contracts with platform-wide error budget math? (proposal: maintain separate per-tenant error budgets tracked in console)
